15:50 < Filip_> that would be great
15:51 < jal0> i plan on implementing a standalone monitor. with basic command for dumping memory regions and modifying register.
16:04 < jal0> hey, just for some though if the companion chip is indeed some form of 4173 then it should have a BCU, if we can find the base address of this register set(by looking for know address) then we can determine a whole slew of other base addresses.
16:04 -!- andreas_ [~chatzilla@ool-43532dca.dyn.optonline.net] has quit ["ChatZilla 0.8.9 [Mozilla rv:1.1/20020908]"]
16:07 < jal0> including the irq status register the piu base address and other info
16:08 < Filip_> butt how can you find it ? has it got a signature ?
16:10 < jal0> should have the NEC PCI vendor id of .. hand on let me find it again
16:10 < Filip_> and how do you get that id ?
16:11 < jal0> they are standardized as part of the PCI spec
16:12 < Filip_> and if nec made a cusom4173, would it havesame id or different ?
16:13 < jal0> http://www.yourvote.com/pci/pciread.asp?sort=fullname
16:15 < jal0> not sure, thats the problem.. but if we know the base address of some devices allready, we can look for that address stored in some memory location. say its the pcu, the buc has the base address of the pcu at offset 0x10 to 0x13
16:15 < jal0> buc=BCU
16:16 < Filip_> the companion chip is labeled by NEC
16:17 < Filip_> intersting: casio has an id, but no known devices
16:17 < jal0> are you asking a question or making a statement?
16:17 < jal0> i would thing that it would be labeled by NEC
16:17 < jal0> not CASIO
16:18 < jal0> device id's are normally hardcoded at production time.
16:19 < jal0> does what i'm saying make any sense to you?
16:20 < Filip_> ys, it does, was just checking the pcb: the companion is indeed labelled by NEC
16:21 < jal0> BASE + 0x0A2 = PIU Control register where BASE is the value stored at location BCU_BASE+0x10
16:21 < jal0> BCU_BASE + 0 should have the VendorId
16:22 < jal0> BCU_BASE+2 = Device Id
16:22 < jal0> BCU_BASE+ 4 = PCI command register
16:22 < jal0> .... etc
16:23 < jal0> so if we find the BCU we can look up the base address for all the other device it acts as a controller for
16:26 < jal0> if we know that what a devices base register is already, we can do a form of reverse lookup to find the BCU_BASE+? wich is a register which hold a pointer to the known address
16:27 < jal0> anyway, just an idea, back to the serial driver now :)
16:29 < jal0> filip: could you give me the values of X2 and X3 crystals
16:29 < jal0> they should be right above the campanion chip
16:30 < Filip_> hold on
16:33 < Filip_> x2: looks like '1VG' but hardly readable
16:34 < jal0> do you have your scope handy?
16:34 < jal0> you should be able to measure them directly
